title: Bina and tevuna: the recap of chapters one and two, and seeing G-d in the shtender
overview:
Rabbi Markel calls chapter three "really a recap chapter": the conclusion of chapters one and two, applied to contemplating G-dliness, with *memalei kol almin*, the coming into being of something from nothing, as the example. Contemplation has two levels. *Bina* is the grasp of the concept itself: its *orech* brings it down into *meshalim*, a physical garment a child could grasp; its *rochav* explains it in many ways; and only after both comes the depth, which looks like the *kitzur* and is not. *Daas* binds the mind to what it understood and brings it to the depth of *chachma* (wisdom), where the mind sees the truth instead of following an explanation.

*Tevuna* brings that depth down into what the eyes see. The Alter Rebbe *davened* "with the *shtender*": he saw that the *shtender* is *Elokus* (G-dliness), as one sees the hidden bunnies once they are pointed out. Without *tevuna* Chassidus stays an abstract puzzle ("What's it good for?"), contemplation in prayer becomes spacing out, and G-d and the world stay two things. The real *tevuna* is *ein od milvado*: you want the health and the money for the Chassidus.

sections.title: Two levels of contemplation; bina is the grasp of the concept itself, down to its depth
sections.summary: The chapter sums up chapters one and two: contemplating G-dliness has two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*. *Bina* is the grasp of the concept itself, in all its details, as with *memalei kol almin*, studied from its outside to its inside until one reaches the *omek hamusag*.

phrases.he: (ג) ובכל זה יובן בענין ההתבוננות
phrases.en: (3) And with all this will be understood the matter of *hisbonenus* (contemplation)

phrases.he: בהשגת האלקות,
phrases.en: in the grasp of G-dliness:

phrases.he: שיש ב' מדריגות, בינה ותבונה.
phrases.en: that there are two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: בינה היינו בחינת עצם ההשגה האלקית בכל פרט
phrases.en: *Bina* is the grasp itself of G-dliness, in every particular

phrases.he: ענין שמתבונן,
phrases.en: matter that one contemplates:

phrases.he: איך הוא
phrases.en: how it is

phrases.he: ומה הוא,
phrases.en: and what it is;

phrases.he: ועומד על הדבר בעיון רב בכל פרטי חלקיו
phrases.en: and he dwells on the thing with much *iyun* (close analysis), in all the details of its parts,

phrases.he: כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: etc., as mentioned above.

blocks.text:
Chapter three is basically the conclusion of chapter two; really it is the conclusion of chapters one and two together. **With all this will be understood** the matter of *hisbonenus* in grasping G-dliness: **there are two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*.**

*Bina* **is the grasp itself of G-dliness, in every particular**, how it is and what it is, gone over **with much *iyun***. In other words, *bina* is the actual learning.

phrases.he: כמו בהשגה פרטיות דממלא כל עלמין
phrases.en: As in the particular grasp of *memalei kol almin* ([the light] that fills all worlds),

phrases.he: שהוא התהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: which is the coming into being of something from nothing,

phrases.he: הנקרא כח הפועל האלקי בנפעל כו'
phrases.en: called the G-dly *koach hapoel banifal* (the power of the maker in the made), etc.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת שם אדנ״י או שם אלהי״ם,
phrases.en: And this is the Name *Adnus* or the Name *Elokim*,

phrases.he: לשון כח כידוע.
phrases.en: words that mean power, as is known.

phrases.he: הנה יש בזה כמה חלוקי פרטים
phrases.en: Now, there are in this a number of distinctions of details

phrases.he: באופני חיצוניות הענין
phrases.en: in the ways of the outside of the matter,

phrases.he: עד אשר יושג תוך תוך הענין הזה
phrases.en: until the very inside of this matter is grasped,

phrases.he: בפנימית העצמי, איך שהוא בעצם כו'
phrases.en: in its inner essence, how it is in its essence, etc.;

phrases.he: שזהו הנקרא עומק המושג כו'
phrases.en: this is what is called the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept), etc.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל שהעיון הוא בחינת כלי
phrases.en: As mentioned above, the *iyun* is a *kli* (vessel)

phrases.he: לבא לבחינת העומק כו'
phrases.en: to come to the depth, etc.

blocks.text: The example is **the particular grasp of *memalei kol almin***, which is **the coming into being of something from nothing**, the *koach hapoel banifal*. **And this is the Name *Adnus* or the Name *Elokim***: both of them **words that mean power**.

blocks.question: Is it the Name Adam here, or *Adnus*?
blocks.text: One book here reads "the Name Adam" (and Adam, he remarks, is *MaH*); another has the letters *alef-dalet*, the Name *Adnus*. Someone suggests: maybe it is "the Name of G-d". One of them is "the old one", and that is what it says there; "but the way you have it, it makes more sense. Actually it makes more sense."

**There are in this a number of distinctions of details in the ways of the outside of the matter**, the matter of *memalei kol almin*, **until the very inside of this matter is grasped**, **how it is in its essence**. **This is what is called the *omek hamusag***.

And, as said above, **the *iyun* is a *kli*** to come to the depth: in other words, to come later on to the whole matter of how the inner [light] works in the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of worlds).

sections.title: Length and breadth: one concept brought close in meshalim and explained in many ways
sections.summary: The *orech* (length) brings the concept down into *meshalim*, a physical garment, until a child could grasp it. The *rochav* (breadth) explains it in many different ways, through spreading forth from the essence and through revealing the hidden, each with many *meshalim* of its own; the opposite of both is the *kitzur*.

phrases.he: ובחינת האורך הוא בחינת התקרבות הענין הזה אל השכל
phrases.en: And the *orech* (length) is bringing this matter close to the *sechel* (intellect)

phrases.he: במשלים שונים הידועים
phrases.en: through the various known *meshalim* (analogies),

phrases.he: עד שיהיה הדבר הזה קרוב במוחו מאד
phrases.en: until the thing is very close in his mind

phrases.he: (בל"א אראפ גילאזן זייער דעם שכל צו זיך)
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: he brings [lit. lowers] the *sechel* very close to himself),

phrases.he: בלבוש הגשמה,
phrases.en: in a physical garment,

phrases.he: עד שיוכל תינוק להשיג כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: until a child could grasp it, etc., as mentioned above.

blocks.text:
**And the *orech* (length) is bringing this matter close to the *sechel* (intellect) through the various known *meshalim* (analogies)**.

Here he does not stop to translate or explain: the author is recapping what he has already said, and it is pretty much self-explanatory.

**Until the thing is very close in his mind.** The Yiddish says it: he brings the *sechel* very close to himself. And it is **in a physical garment**: the *meshalim* are the physical garment, **until a child could grasp it**, like this thing, as above.

phrases.he: והרוחב היינו להרחיב זה הדבר כמו שהוא בכמה אופנים שונים,
phrases.en: And the *rochav* (breadth) is to broaden this thing, as it is, in a number of different ways,

phrases.he: ולא באופן א' לבד
phrases.en: and not in one way alone,

phrases.he: כמו המשל לזה הדבר מחיי הנפש בגוף,
phrases.en: like the *mashal* for this thing from the life of the soul in the body,

phrases.he: שאין זה רק התפשטות מן העצם כידוע
phrases.en: which is only a *hispashtus min ha'etzem* (spreading forth from the essence), as is known.

blocks.text: **And the *rochav* (breadth) is to broaden this thing, as it is, in a number of different ways, and not in one way alone**. For instance **the *mashal* for this thing from the life of the soul in the body**: the life of the soul in the body is a *hispashtus min ha'etzem*.

phrases.he: ויש רבוי אופנים למאוד בהתפשטות מן העצם
phrases.en: And there are very many ways in spreading forth from the essence,

phrases.he: וגם בגלוי ההעלם,
phrases.en: and also in *gilui ha'helem* (revealing the hidden),

phrases.he: כתנועת החי וכאותיות הדבור כו'
phrases.en: like the movement of a living creature, and like the letters of speech, etc.,

phrases.he: או כהתחכמות מן עצם החכמה
phrases.en: or like the reasoning that comes from the essence of *chachma*,

phrases.he: או כגלוי הראיה דעין
phrases.en: or like the revealing of the sight of the eye,

phrases.he: או כגלוי שלהבת מן הגחלת כו'
phrases.en: or like the revealing of a flame from the coal, etc.;

phrases.he: וכל זה נקרא גלוי ההעלם
phrases.en: and all this is called revealing the hidden.

blocks.text: **There are very many ways in spreading forth from the essence**: various *meshalim* for it. **And also in *gilui ha'helem*.** So there are a few ways in which the matter of *memalei kol almin* is explained. One is the way of spreading forth from the essence, which itself has a bunch of *meshalim*. Another way is revealing the hidden.

And revealing the hidden too comes in various ways: **like the movement of a living creature, and like the letters of speech**; **or like the reasoning that comes from the essence of *chachma***, **or like the revealing of the sight of the eye, or like the revealing of a flame from the coal**. Each one is a different way of saying it, or of explaining it. **And all this is called revealing the hidden**: all of it is the *rochav* of one *orech*, the *orech* of revealing the hidden.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן משל זיו השמש
phrases.en: Whereas the *mashal* of the sun's radiance,

phrases.he: או אור הנר וכח הפועל כו'
phrases.en: or the light of a candle, and the power of the maker, etc.,

phrases.he: שנקרא התפשטות כו' וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: is called spreading forth, etc., and the like.

phrases.he: הרי כל זה בעצם הענין
phrases.en: All this is in the essence of the matter,

phrases.he: רק שנתרחב,
phrases.en: only it has been broadened.

phrases.he: וההיפך מזה הוא הקיצור רק באופן אחד,
phrases.en: And the opposite of this is the *kitzur* (shortening), in one way only,

phrases.he: וגם הוא בדרך קצרה
phrases.en: and also in a short way,

phrases.he: נסקר במוחו בלתי התפשטות להרחיב בו כלל כו'
phrases.en: glanced over in his mind, without spreading out to broaden it at all, etc.

blocks.text: **Whereas the *mashal* of the sun's radiance, or the light of a candle, and the power of the maker** is **called spreading forth** from the essence. That is a different *orech*, and it too has various ways to explain it, and so on.

**All this is in the essence of the matter**: all of it is still about the essence of the matter of *memalei kol almin*, **only it has been broadened**. **And the opposite of this is the *kitzur* (shortening), in one way only**, which means narrow; **and also in a short way**, short in length. So the *kitzur* is a shortness of breadth and a shortness of length: the thing **glanced over in his mind, without spreading out to broaden it at all**.

sections.title: The depth comes only after length and breadth, in every concept of G-dliness
sections.summary: The depth reached after all the *meshalim* and explanations looks like the *kitzur* and is not. Everything chapter one said of *Keser* (crown), *chachma* and *bina* of *bina* is found in a particular concept like *memalei kol almin*, and in every particular of G-dliness the book will explain.

phrases.he: אבל כמו שזה הדבר נתפס לעומקו בעצם,
phrases.en: But as this thing is grasped to its depth, in essence,

phrases.he: אחר כל רבוי הסבר דמיון המשלים,
phrases.en: after all the many explanations and likenesses of the *meshalim*,

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא עומק ותמצית זה המושג כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is what is called the depth and essence of this concept, as mentioned above.

phrases.he: ודווקא אחר האריכות והרוחב במשלים בעיון רב
phrases.en: And *davka* after the length and the breadth in *meshalim*, with much *iyun*,

phrases.he: יבא לבחינת העומק שמובן מהם,
phrases.en: he will come to the depth that is understood from them

phrases.he: (בל"א דער הערין דיא טיפקייט פון דעם וויא דיא זאך איז באמת)
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: to perceive the real depth of it, how the thing truly is),

phrases.he: דהיינו אחר הלבשת חיצוניותו בכל העיון הרב כו'
phrases.en: that is, after it has been dressed on its outside in all the great *iyun*, etc.;

phrases.he: ודי למבין
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **But**: so that, by the way, is the *kitzur*, the *kitzur* [mentioned] before. **As this thing is grasped to its depth, in essence, after all the many explanations and likenesses of the *meshalim***, **that is what is called the depth and essence of this concept.** It looks the same as the *kitzur*, but it really is not.

**And *davka* after the length and the breadth in *meshalim*, with much *iyun*, he will come to the depth that is understood from them**: like the thing that was said about the Alter Rebbe, or the Deitschel and the dead man. In Yiddish: **to perceive the real depth of it, how the thing truly is**, the real deepness of this thing, how the thing really is. **That is, after it has been dressed on its outside in all the great *iyun*.**

So basically, in this one passage, he has just recapped chapter one.

phrases.he: (וכל מה שכתבנו למעלה בכל פרטי כח''ב דבינה,
phrases.en: (And all that we wrote above in all the details of *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *bina*,

phrases.he: הכל ימצא בהשגה פרטיות כזאת,
phrases.en: all of it will be found in a particular grasp like this,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא בכל השגת אלקות הפרטים9 וכמשי"ת)
phrases.en: and the same in every grasp of the particulars of G-dliness, as will be explained.)

blocks.text: Up to now he has explained the matter of *bina* and applied it to *memalei kol almin*. In the way of *memalei kol almin*, the *bina* of it is to go through it and understand it with all the details, with all the different *meshalim* and all the different explanations, whether it is spreading forth or revealing; that is the breadth. And the length is to bring each thing down into *meshalim*: for instance, revealing the hidden is like the letters of speech, which reveal the letters of thought. That is a *mashal*. Or like the *mashal* of a river. The length is to bring it down into physical terms.

**And all that we wrote above in all the details of *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *bina***: the whole thing was explained above, in chapter one. The *bina* of *bina* is the *hisbonenus*; the *chachma* of *bina* is to discover a new thing within the same thing; the *Keser* is the *omek hamusag*; and then there is the deeper *Keser*, of the *shaar hanun* (the fiftieth gate).

**All of it will be found in a particular grasp like this**: in any particular grasp throughout the book you will find this whole matter of the understanding, the *bina* of the thing. **And the same**, as you find it in the matter of *memalei kol almin*, **in every grasp of the particulars of G-dliness, as will be explained** later in the book. So he has recapped what the matter of *bina* is.

sections.title: Daas: the bond with the concept, and the depth of chachma, where the mind sees
sections.summary: *Daas* is recognising and feeling what one has understood, bound to it; the mitzva to know G-d is *davka* in *memalei kol almin*. It brings to the depth of *chachma*, the *re'iyas hasechel*, where one no longer follows an explanation but sees the truth of it.

phrases.he: ובחי' הדעת הוא בחינת ההכרה והרגשה במושכל
phrases.en: And *daas* is the recognition and feeling of the *muskal* (the thing understood),

phrases.he: בהתקשרות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: with a bond, as mentioned above.

phrases.he: ועל זה נאמר וידעת כו'
phrases.en: And of this it is said, "And you shall know," etc.,

phrases.he: דע את אלה״י כו'
phrases.en: "Know the G-d [of your father]," etc.,

phrases.he: שהוא בהשגה זו דממלא כל עלמין דוקא כידוע
phrases.en: which is *davka* in this grasp of *memalei kol almin*, as is known.

blocks.text: **And *daas* is the recognition and feeling of the *muskal* (the thing understood), with a bond**, as he explained before. **And of this it is said, "And you shall know,"** and **"Know the G-d [of your father]"**: this matter of the mitzva of *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d) is *davka* in the matter of *memalei kol almin*. That is one of the things meant by "the earth shall be full of knowledge of G-d as the waters cover the sea."

So basically he is telling you now that *daas Havaya* is *davka* in the *seder hishtalshelus*, in *memalei kol almin*. And Rabbi Markel thinks that if you look at it even closer, the real *daas Havaya* is really *davka* in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, more than in the actual higher-up thing. Even so, *Havaya* is basically the four worlds, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. That is the matter of *daas*.
So *daas* is *davka* in the grasp: to be bound to it, to have *daas* enter the grasp, *davka* the *daas Havaya* of *memalei kol almin*. And in Yiddish, as the text goes on, *der klepp*.

phrases.he: (בל"א דער קלעפ כו' כנ"ל באורך)
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: *der klepp* (the holding on), etc., as above at length),

phrases.he: שהוא דוקא המביא לבחינת עומקא דכולא,
phrases.en: which is *davka* what brings to the *omka d'chula* (the depth of everything),

phrases.he: דהיינו לעומק דחכמה שמאין תמצא כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is, to the depth of *chachma*, "which is found from nothing," as mentioned above;

phrases.he: דהיינו בבחינת עומק ראיות השכל
phrases.en: that is, in the depth of the *re'iyas hasechel* (the sight of the intellect)

phrases.he: בהשגה זו דבחינת מלא כל עלמין
phrases.en: in this grasp of [the light that] fills all worlds,

phrases.he: שלמעלה מהשגת השכל כידוע
phrases.en: which is above the intellect's grasp, as is known.

blocks.text: ***Der klepp***: he thinks *klepp* is the holding on, *davka* in the length of the thing. **Which is *davka* what brings to the *omka d'chula***: it is *davka* the *hisbonenus* that brings to the depth of everything. Meaning what? **The depth of *chachma***, the *taalumos chachma* (the hidden depths of wisdom) he explained before, which come after the *hisbonenus*, **"which is found from nothing."**

**That is, in the depth of the *re'iyas hasechel***: when you see the thing with your mind. This seeing is not like the seeing of prophecy. The seeing of prophecy is to see *mamash* with the eyes. *Re'iyas hasechel* means that I explain something to you enough, until you see the truth of it. You *mamash* see the truth of it. It is not an explanation anymore: you actually see the truth of it.

blocks.question: The Rebbe says that even a physical seeing will come out of *hisbonenus*. Is that what is meant here?
blocks.text: Physical sight does come out of *hisbonenus*; everything comes out of *hisbonenus*. But what he is talking about here is *re'iyas hasechel*. The student presses: when the Rebbe says in the *sicha* (talk) that one points with the finger and says "this", that is not with *re'iyas hasechel*, that is *davka* with physical sight. "That's what I said." That is seeing with the eyes, and that is not what he is talking about here. He is talking about the *re'iyas hasechel*, which is called the seeing of *chachma*.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב ברעיא מהימנא,
phrases.en: (And as it is written in the *Ra'aya Mehemna*:

phrases.he: בעין בשכל, דבלבא אתחזי כולא,
phrases.en: "with the eye of the intellect, in the heart everything is seen,"

phrases.he: ונקרא לאסתכלא ביקרא כו'
phrases.en: and this is called "to gaze at the glory [of the King]," etc.

phrases.he: וגם בזה יש בחינת עומק כנזכר לעיל באריכות)
phrases.en: And in this too there is depth, as mentioned above at length.)

blocks.text:
**As it is written in the *Ra'aya Mehemna***: with the eye of the *sechel* within the heart, everything is seen. **And this is called "to gaze at the glory [of the King]"**: to see the glory of the King. **And in this too there is depth**: as explained before, when you get to *chachma* there is also a length and a breadth and a depth, so in the seeing of *chachma* there is also a depth.

That is the matter of chapter one, up to here.

sections.title: Tevuna: bringing the hidden depth down until you see G-d in the world
sections.summary: *Tevuna* draws the hidden depth of the concept down into revelation, all the way into what the eyes see, so that one sees the world itself as G-dliness, like the hidden bunnies in a picture once someone points them out. One who has absorbed the concept can bring it into the details of how each created thing comes into being.

phrases.he: ובחינת התבונה
phrases.en: And *tevuna*

phrases.he: היינו לדלות על ידו מעומק זה הנעלם
phrases.en: is to draw up through it from this hidden depth

phrases.he: במושג זה דממלא כל עלמין הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: in this concept of *memalei kol almin* mentioned above

phrases.he: לידי גילוי,
phrases.en: into revelation.

blocks.text: Now he is getting to chapter two. **And *tevuna***: what is the thing of *tevuna*? Remember, the whole exile is *davka* because of the lack of *tevuna*. It is a lack of *bina* too; it says "My people does not contemplate," and really both of them are missing, but it is even more the lack of *tevuna*.

*Tevuna* **is to draw up through it from this hidden depth**. Once you get to the hidden depth, it means not just the depth of *bina* but the depth of *chachma*: where you get to the point that you *mamash* see the verity of the explanation. Not that you see the explanation; through the explanation you see how it actually is, in a mental way. *Tevuna* brings it **into revelation**.

And this, by the way, is where the actual seeing with the eye comes in: to bring it down so that you can *mamash* see the G-dliness in the physical world, in what is actually happening, so that when you see the physical world... (here a phone call cuts him off).
He reads it again: *tevuna* draws it up **into revelation**. And as he said, the real seeing with the eyes is like that.

blocks.title: "With the shtender"
blocks.text:
To have the *tevuna* means that once you understand the whole understanding, it is no longer just an abstract thing: you bring it all the way down into the actuality of what you are seeing, and you see.

There is a story of the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe. The Alter Rebbe asked the Mitteler Rebbe, "What did you *daven* with?" And he told him that he *davened* with a *hisbonenus* about *Adam Kadmon*. Then he asked the Alter Rebbe, "And what did you *daven* with?" And the Alter Rebbe told him: "With the *shtender*."

What does it mean, with the *shtender*? He was holding on to the *shtender*, that's how he *davened*? Did he mean it like a joke? No. He *davened* with the actual fact that he saw that the *shtender* itself is *Elokus*. That is *tevuna*: to look around and apply that whole thing of the *bina*, and realise that you are looking at nothing but G-d, *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him). You are actually looking at G-d right now. And not only are you looking at G-d: you were looking at Him the whole time. The thing is that you know how to parse it.

blocks.title: Find the ten bunnies
blocks.text:
This is basically, as you say, to see. So what, do you see G-d more than somebody else sees G-d? Somebody else is seeing the same physical world that you are seeing.

It is like "find the ten bunnies". These little kiddie puzzles they have in kiddie magazines ("Like 'Find Waldo'?" "Whatever"): there is a picture, and you have to find the ten bunnies in it. They are hidden. There is a tree, and if you look at the leaves you see there is a bunny there. It looks like leaves, and then you look closely and you see, oh, there's an upside-down bunny over there. And the cartoons they have in the newspapers.

blocks.title: Once you see the bunny
blocks.text: When you look at the picture, you are seeing the ten bunnies. You are just not aware of them; but you are seeing them. You saw them the same before you found the ten bunnies and after you found them. But after you found them, right away you say, "You see, there it is." And not only that: before, it looked to you just like a bunch of leaves, and once you have found the bunny it is hard to make it look like leaves again. Like with these optical illusions: once you see it properly, it is hard not to see it properly anymore.

Over here it is also a thing like "You are a G-d who hides": He is hiding. But once you see it, or if somebody else will show it to you: "Where are ten bunnies?" "Here, look, you see over here? There's his nose and there's his feet." "Oh, yeah." That is basically what the Rebbe [the author] is going to show us in this book: where the ten bunnies are. And once you see it, you say, "Oh, yeah."

But even before, when you looked at the picture, you saw everything there is to see in the picture. So how come you didn't see the bunny? You didn't notice it. And really, after somebody told you where the bunnies are, you are not seeing more than you saw before. You are seeing exactly the same picture you saw before, and yet now you see the bunnies with your physical eyes. It is not just an explanation they told you: the explanation tells you that in this picture there are ten bunnies. The same with an explanation, when people tell you: "You see this picture in front of your eyes right now? There's ten bunnies there." "Well, where are they?"

But now you will see: here is His hand, *chesed* the right arm; here is the other hand, *gevura* the left arm. And you can say, "Oh right, here's the hand of G-d." As it says that when the Jews went up out of Egypt, the magicians saw the finger of G-d, and later on they saw the hand of G-d. So what did they see? They did not see anything. They did not see any hand; but they saw a thing that was the hand of G-d.

**For since he takes in the essence of this grasp thoroughly**: in other words, it is not enough to understand the matter of what he is going to explain to us here. You have to go over it a few more times, until you absorb it. Then **he can therefore bring it into a number of matters separate from it**.

sections.title: Without tevuna Chassidus is a puzzle on the side: "What's it good for?"
sections.summary: Without *tevuna* the concept stays in the mind and a person does not know what to do with it, even though he understood it well; he thinks contemplation in prayer means spacing out on abstract things, when prayer is bringing G-d down into the world. For him G-d and the world are two things; the real *tevuna* is *ein od milvado*, where what one really wants is the Chassidus itself.

phrases.he: ובלתי כח התבונה הזאת בהשגה זו שממלא כל עלמין
phrases.en: And without this power of *tevuna* in this grasp of *memalei kol almin*,

phrases.he: הרי נשארת השגה זו רק במוח הבנתו לבד,
phrases.en: this grasp remains only in the mind of his understanding, alone,

phrases.he: ולא ידע מה לעשות בה
phrases.en: and he does not know what to do with it,

phrases.he: ואיך להביא זאת ההתבוננות באיכות ענין התהוות היש מאין כלל,
phrases.en: or how to bring this *hisbonenus* into how the coming into being of something from nothing actually is, at all,

phrases.he: כמובן מכל הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין
phrases.en: as is understood from all that was said above; and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **Without this power of *tevuna* in this grasp of *memalei kol almin***: we see that there is a whole bunch of people all over the place studying Chassidus, and yet they don't have no *tevuna* in it. Why? **This grasp remains only in the mind of his understanding, alone, and he does not know what to do with it.**

Like people say: "So let's say you learn *Ayin Beis*. What's it good for? Is it going to make me any money? Is it going to improve my *middos* (character traits)? If I read a *mussar* (ethical teaching) book, it will improve my *middos*. But what is this? It's just an intellectual thing. It's good for people who like to do mathematical acrostic puzzles. What do you do with it?" Or they say: to *daven*, how does this help with the *davenen*?

**Or how to bring this *hisbonenus* into how the coming into being of something from nothing actually is**: how to bring this whole *hisbonenus* into an actual understanding of how the actual world comes to be something from nothing, rather than just a bunch of abstract explanations.

phrases.he: (ומזה מובן סיבת המניעה בחדשים או גם בישנים
phrases.en: (And from this is understood the reason for what holds back the new ones, or the old ones too,

phrases.he: בחסרי תבונה,

phrases.he: גם שמשיגים היטב הדק בשעה ששומעים ורואים,

blocks.text: **From this is understood the reason for what holds back the new ones, or the old ones too.** Why? Because they **lack *tevuna***. **Even though they grasp it well and finely at the time they hear and see it**: they learned Chassidus and they understood it. They understood the *sichos* (talks), whatever; maybe not every last detail, but they understood something there. Still, **they cannot bring the thing at all into *hisbonenus* in *tefilla***: not necessarily in *tefilla*, but *hisbonenus* in terms of an actual relationship to the world.

And by the way, in terms of *tefilla* too: when people think of *hisbonenus* in *tefilla*, they think it means that during the *tefilla* they will think about abstract things. That's what *hisbonenus* means to them. So they will sit there in the *tefilla* and space out.

But the height of the whole *tefilla* is that you are asking the *Aibershter* (the One Above): "Make me healthy. Give me money. Bring us back to Jerusalem. Build the Temple." ("Exactly.") That is the height of the whole *tefilla*. In other words, *tefilla* means you are asking the *Aibershter* to connect. As they say, "Blessed are You": bring Yourself down to here. *Baruch* (blessed) means to bring down, like *bereicha* (a pool).

So: bring Yourself down to here. Bring the dead back to life. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned. Then you say, what do you call it: give us a livelihood. Give us health. Bring us back to Jerusalem, and rebuild the Temple, and bring back the service into the Temple, and we can all sit and learn Chassidus the whole time.

Their whole thing, because they have no *tevuna*, is that they think *hisbonenus* in the *tefilla* means that you will sit and space out on these abstract things. When really *tefilla* means that you are going to bring G-dliness down into the world, and you are asking for it to come in terms of actual physical things. Basically the *tefilla* is part of asking the *Aibershter* to take over the world. ("Exactly.") That's what it says there: to bring Moshiach and take over the world. There's a prayer for that, and stuff like that.

And they don't understand: what does the *hisbonenus* of how *Atik* and *Arich* (Atik Yomin and Arich Anpin, levels of *Keser*) are two sides of the same thing have to do with "I'm going to get money"? What does it have to do with anything?

He is talking here about *avodas halev* (the service of the heart) and *tefilla*, and even *avodas hamochin*, and certainly *daas Havaya*, which will be the real thing of Moshiach. It is not just during the *tefilla*. In everything that you do, you are supposed to see that this is not some accidental thing that is happening: it is literally the *Aibershter* doing it all. You are supposed to see that, not just believe it. There is the matter of belief in *hashgacha pratis* (divine providence); and this is that you are supposed to see it, actually see it. So even though they understand it fine, they have no understanding [of what to do with it].

phrases.he: (בל"א מער ניט „ז דער מושכל15 „ליין פ„ר זיך כו')
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: nothing more than the *muskal* alone, by itself, etc.);

phrases.he: וד"ל16:
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **Until he asks, What is one to do with all this?** What am I going to do with all this Chassidus? What's it good for? **For what use does one need this?** What do I need this for?

And really there is an even higher thing. It is not that the Chassidus is for the money: when you are asking for a livelihood, the Chassidus is the livelihood. That is the whole thing he wants. The main thing he wants is *davka* the Chassidus itself; not "what do I need the Chassidus for, in order to get the other things?" He knows that the Chassidus is the main thing he needs, and if anything, the money is for the Chassidus.

Why? **For in his mind they are two separate things**: the Chassidus and the world are, by him, two different things that have nothing to do with each other. There's a world and there's Chassidus. The world is the world, and on Shabbos you go and sit with your friends and play a crossword puzzle of Chassidus a little bit, and that's it. They have nothing to do with each other. Why? **Because only the understanding itself remains in his mind, completely separate from any matter.**

In Yiddish: **nothing more than the *muskal* alone, by itself**. Nothing but the idea itself is what he has; and the idea is not connected to anything. **And this is enough for one who understands**: just a bunch of abstract thoughts with absolutely no relationship to anything, to the world, to his life.

And not just that. The other thing he says here, "two separate things by him", means there are various levels. In one it is totally abstract, and it has nothing to do even with the things in the *tefilla*. In the other it has to do with bringing down the light into things so that you will get things in the world; but it is still two different things. There's G-d and there's the world, and you are asking G-d to help you. You already have some *tevuna*, that something is going to come out of it. That is not the real *tevuna*.

The real *tevuna* is the *ein od milvado*: what you really want is the Chassidus. The whole reason you want the health is not that you want the Chassidus to help you with the health. It's the opposite: you want the health, and the money, to help you with the Chassidus. Like if we were all healthy and had a whole bunch of money, we could all sit together and learn Chassidus all the time. And it's all one thing.

And well, we did a whole chapter. This was really a recap chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the *orech* and the *rochav* of *bina*, and what is the *kitzur* that is the opposite of both?
Why are the movement of a creature, the letters of speech and the flame from the coal the *rochav* of one *orech*?
If the depth reached after length and breadth looks like the *kitzur*, how is it different?
How is the *re'iyas hasechel* different from the seeing of prophecy, and from pointing with a finger and saying "this"?
What did the Alter Rebbe mean when he said he *davened* "with the *shtender*", and what do the ten bunnies add?
Why do people who understand Chassidus well still ask "What's it good for?", and what is the real *tevuna* about health, money and Chassidus?

notes.text: Line 4: he reads "shem Adam" (and remarks "Adam is MaH"); a student's book has alef-dalet (Ad-nai). He has "the old one" and says the other reading "makes more sense". Who holds which book is not certain from the transcript; the phrases follow the printed text (Adnus).

Line 5: the half-sentence after "the iyun is a kli" (021 w212-233) is broken ("the iyun into, in other words, later on the whole inyan of how the pnimi works in the seder hishtalshelus"); the block renders it as "to come later on to how the inner [light] works in the seder hishtalshelus". Check against the audio.

Line 15: "like the thing we said about the Alter Rebbe or the Deitschel and the mes" (021 w656-671) points back to a story told in an earlier class (probably one of the chapter 10-15 classes recorded first); it is not told here, and the block keeps only the reference.

Line 22: the sentence ending at 021 w1712 ("so that when you see the physical world, Hello, Shimon?") is cut off by the phone call; the block leaves it unfinished. The story of the shtender is introduced at the end of the sentence w1777-1836, so the story's audio starts at w1777 with his tevuna lead-in.
Line 19: he reads "der klepp" tentatively ("I think klepp is the holding onto..."); reported as his reading.

Lines 19-20: "the Rebbe" in the student's question (021 w1325-1418), with the talk about pointing with a finger, is presumably the Lubavitcher Rebbe; at w2367 "what the Rebbe is going to show us in this book" is the author, marked [the author].

Line 22: he says the magicians saw the finger of G-d "when the Jews went up out of Egypt" and "later on they saw the hand of G-d". In the verses the magicians say "the finger of G-d" at the plague of lice (Exodus 8:15), and Israel sees "the great hand" at the sea (Exodus 14:31). The block keeps what he said.

Line 22: the alignment mark (conf 0.42) is at w1740, but he starts tevuna at w1513 ("Now he's getting to chapter two"); all of w1513-2702 is under this line. His rereading at w2650 is garbled ("ki b'yeser kelipas hachitzonim"); the phrase "for since he takes in the essence of this grasp thoroughly" follows the printed text and his explanation ("go over it a few more times till you absorb it").

Lines 6, 7, 25-26: he reads some words differently from the printed text (line 6 "hesbaras" (explaining) for "hiskarvus" (bringing close); line 7 the Yiddish "er hot gebracht" (he brought) for "arop gelozn" (lowered, let down), which the phrase marks as [lit. lowers]; "hachiluk" for "hadak", "ad shetishaer" for "ad sheyishal", "shenishar rak bechinas avoda atzma umocho nivdal"); the phrases follow the printed text. He translates hardly any of lines 1-21 phrase by phrase ("I'm not translating or explaining because... he's recapping"); there the phrases are a plain rendering in the words of his explanation.

No block is flagged for sensitivity: the class has no remark about women, other religions, politics or a named person. The sharpest remarks (people "all over the place studying Chassidus" with no tevuna, sitting in prayer and spacing out, the Shabbos "crossword puzzle of Chassidus") are criticism of an attitude, not of a group, and are kept as he said them.
